Measure (Article 21(2) of Directive (EU): Policies on risk analysis and information system security
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 controls that address: 5.1 Policies for information security; 5.2 Information security roles and responsibilities; 5.4 Management responsibilities; 5.36 Compliance with policies; ISMS clauses 6.1.2, 6.1.3, 8.2, 8.3
Gap that stays open: The ISMS requires an approved policy and a documented risk method, but not that the management body approves the NIS2 measures (Article 20) and not that the risk picture covers the services that put the entity in scope; the certification scope can stop short of part of the entity
Evidence that closes the gap: Approved security policy with a review date; risk register with owners and treatment dates; board minute approving the measures; ISMS scope statement naming every in-scope service
Typical owner: CISO together with the board member designated under Article 20

ISO/IEC 27001:2022 controls that address: 5.24 Information security incident management planning and preparation; 5.25 Assessment and decision on information security events; 5.26 Response to information security incidents; 5.27 Learning from incidents; 5.28 Collection of evidence; 6.8 Information security event reporting; 8.15 Logging; 8.16 Monitoring activities
Gap that stays open: The standard requires a handling process, not an external notification: the 24-hour early warning, 72-hour incident notification and one-month final report to the CSIRT or competent authority (Article 23) have no counterpart in Annex A
Evidence that closes the gap: Runbook with the 24-hour and 72-hour steps, recipients and content; incident log with timestamps from detection to notification; one exercise or real notification; evidence that the addressee was the correct CSIRT

Measure (Article 21(2) of Directive (EU): Business continuity, backup, disaster recovery and crisis management
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 controls that address: 5.29 Information security during disruption; 5.30 ICT readiness for business continuity; 8.13 Information backup; 8.14 Redundancy of information processing facilities
Gap that stays open: Continuity is framed around information security during disruption, not around the regulated service; neither document fixes an RTO, an RPO or a restore-test cadence, and crisis communication to authorities and customers is outside Annex A
Evidence that closes the gap: Restore test log with dates and durations against stated RTO and RPO; continuity plan per critical service; crisis contact list including the CSIRT and the competent authority

Measure (Article 21(2) of Directive (EU): Supply chain security, including the security aspects of the relationship with each direct supplier
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 controls that address: 5.19 Information security in supplier relationships; 5.20 Addressing information security within supplier agreements; 5.21 Managing information security in the ICT supply chain; 5.22 Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services; 5.23 Information security for use of cloud services
Gap that stays open: Annex A gives the framework and requires agreed security clauses, but there is no criticality ranking and no minimum clause set; Article 21(3) additionally requires the vulnerabilities specific to each direct supplier, and the quality of their products and secure development practices, to be taken into account
Evidence that closes the gap: Supplier register with a criticality flag per supplier; due diligence notes for every critical supplier; contract clauses on incident notification and audit rights; review dates

Measure (Article 21(2) of Directive (EU): Security in acquisition, development and maintenance, including vulnerability handling and disclosure
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 controls that address: 8.8 Management of technical vulnerabilities; 8.25 Secure development life cycle; 8.26 Application security requirements; 8.27 Secure system architecture and engineering principles; 8.28 Secure coding; 8.29 Security testing in development and acceptance; 8.31 Separation of development, test and production environments; 8.32 Change management; 8.4 Access to source code
Gap that stays open: Development, change control and vulnerability remediation are covered; vulnerability disclosure is a legal element with no Annex A control behind it, and remediation deadlines are set by the entity rather than by an external requirement
Evidence that closes the gap: Vulnerability register with remediation dates and closures; patch window per severity; published security contact and a disclosure process; recent scan or penetration test report; change records

Measure (Article 21(2) of Directive (EU): Policies and procedures to assess the effectiveness of the cybersecurity risk-management measures
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 controls that address: 5.35 Independent review of information security; 5.36 Compliance with policies, rules and standards; 8.34 Protection of information systems during audit testing; ISMS clauses 9.1, 9.2, 9.3
Gap that stays open: Effectiveness is judged internally and by the certification body; the supervisor judges it under its own powers, and the internal audit programme, its scope and its metrics are chosen by the entity
Evidence that closes the gap: Internal audit programme and reports; management review minutes; effectiveness metrics with results; corrective action tracker showing closures

Measure (Article 21(2) of Directive (EU): Basic cyber hygiene practices and cybersecurity training
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 controls that address: 6.3 Information security awareness, education and training; 5.10 Acceptable use of information and other associated assets; 7.7 Clear desk and clear screen; 8.7 Protection against malware; 8.19 Installation of software on operational systems
Gap that stays open: Annex A requires awareness and training without fixing frequency, audience or content; management-body training under Article 20(2) is a separate duty, and basic cyber hygiene is not defined by the standard
Evidence that closes the gap: Training matrix by role with completion records; phishing or tabletop exercise results; board training record with date, content and attendees

Measure (Article 21(2) of Directive (EU): Policies and procedures on the use of cryptography and, where appropriate, encryption
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 controls that address: 8.24 Use of cryptography; 5.14 Information transfer; 5.17 Authentication information; 8.5 Secure authentication
Gap that stays open: 8.24 requires a policy including key management, but neither document names algorithms or states which data and channels must be encrypted; the applicable baseline comes from sector guidance or the regulator
Evidence that closes the gap: Cryptographic inventory covering data at rest, data in transit and key custody; key management procedure; configuration baseline; approved exception list

Measure (Article 21(2) of Directive (EU): Human resources security, access control policies and asset management
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 controls that address: 6.1 Screening; 6.2 Terms and conditions of employment; 6.4 Disciplinary process; 6.5 Responsibilities after termination or change of employment; 6.6 Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements; 6.7 Remote working; 5.9 Inventory of information and other associated assets; 5.11 Return of assets; 5.15 Access control; 5.16 Identity management; 5.17 Authentication information; 5.18 Access rights; 8.1 User endpoint devices; 8.2 Privileged access rights; 8.3 Information access restriction
Gap that stays open: The densest part of Annex A and the easiest to evidence; the residual gap is coverage rather than substance, because the inventory and the access model only have to cover what the certificate covers, while NIS2 follows the service
Evidence that closes the gap: Asset and identity inventories; joiner-mover-leaver records; privileged access review minutes; offboarding and asset return records

Measure (Article 21(2) of Directive (EU): Multi-factor authentication or continuous authentication, secured voice, video and text communications, and secured emergency communication systems
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 controls that address: 8.5 Secure authentication; 5.17 Authentication information; 5.14 Information transfer; 6.7 Remote working; 8.20 Networks security; 8.21 Security of network services
Gap that stays open: Secure authentication is required, but MFA is not framed as a named duty with a defined coverage surface, and secured emergency communication is only implied; Article 21(2)(j) is qualified by where appropriate, so the entity has to document the decision
Evidence that closes the gap: MFA coverage report for remote and privileged access; list of admin consoles and service-provider portals with MFA state; emergency communication plan with tested out-of-band contacts
